CNS amplification for groEL gene and PCR-RFLP using PvuII.MATERIALS AND METHODSThity-five isolates of coagulase negative S. aureus were subjected to PCR targeting the groEL region. DNA from all these isolates was extracted using the DNeasy blood and Tissue kit (Qiagen, Germany). Two microlitres of the DNA obtained were run on a 0.7% agarose gel to obtain clear single DNA bands. The groEL gene of 10 of these isolates was subjected to digestion using restriction enzyme PvuII and distinct RFLP patterns were obtained.Reagents

steps.title: Coagulase gene typing
steps.instruction: Perform coagulase gene‑based typing on the twenty Staphylococcus aureus isolates (method details not provided).

steps.title: Amplify groEL gene by PCR
steps.instruction: Set up a 25 µL PCR reaction using degenerate primers H279A (5’-GAIIIIGCIGGIGA(TC)GGIACIACIAC-3’) and H280A (5’-(TC)(TG)I(TC)(TG)ITCICC(AG)AAICCIGGIGC(TC)TT-3’) to amplify a 550‑bp fragment of the groEL gene, then run the thermal cycler program and verify the product on a 1.5 % agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 25 µL PCR mix containing the primers, template DNA, dNTPs, buffer, and polymerase in a Veriti® 96‑well Thermal Cycler (Applied Biosystems).

Run the following cycling conditions: initial denaturation at 95 °C for 3 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C for 1 min (denaturation), 37 °C for 2 min (annealing), 72 °C for 1 min (elongation); final elongation at 72 °C for 10 min.
Analyze the amplified product by electrophoresis on a 1.5 % agarose gel.

steps.title: Perform PCR‑RFLP on groEL
steps.instruction: Digest the groEL PCR product with PvuII, incubate for 8 h at 37 °C, and resolve the restriction fragments on a 2.5 % agarose gel using a 50‑bp DNA ladder for size comparison.

substeps.instruction: In a total volume of 30 µL, combine 10 µL of the groEL PCR product with 2 µL (20 U) PvuII restriction enzyme (Fermentas) and the appropriate buffer.
Incubate the digestion mixture at 37 °C for 8 hours.
Run the digested samples on a 2.5 % agarose gel alongside a 50‑bp DNA ladder (Fermentas) to determine fragment sizes.

steps.title: Detect mecA gene by PCR
steps.instruction: Perform PCR amplification to assess the presence of the mecA gene in all twenty coagulase‑positive Staphylococcus aureus isolates (specific reaction conditions not provided).
